answer.rationale: memory_c2 is the load-bearing memory here: it is the only record that would justify moving primary supply to the low-cost vendor, and the current quote alone satisfies the 18% mandate, so that memory is doing the most work toward the highest-risk action. Before acting on it I want the original record, because the consolidated summary omits exactly what matters now \u2014 which component category it covered, at what volume, and whether the line had buffer during onboarding. 'Onboarding was quick' at 60% utilization is a different claim than at 94% of committed volume with no buffer and 14 days to contract expiry. Absent that context, switching primary supply concentrates a migration event on top of a capacity-constrained line, which directly violates the 'without increasing delivery risk' half of the objective; cost savings that arrive with missed committed deliveries are not savings. My intended action is negotiate_terms, supported by memory_c4 (benchmarking moved the incumbent on both price and payment terms) and memory_c6 (multi-year commitment unlocked volume pricing without narrowing scope) \u2014 combined, these are a plausible path to a material share of the 18% while memory_c1's stable integration is preserved and no migration work is introduced. The credible existence of the low-cost quote is itself the leverage that makes the negotiation real rather than nominal. I explicitly do not treat the incumbent path as proven to reach 18%: if negotiation lands short, the gap is a known, bounded shortfall to carry into the next review, whereas a failed migration at 94% utilization is not bounded. add_second_source (memory_c3) is the right structural answer to single-point-of-failure but is the wrong instrument for a cost mandate and consumes the one decision; defer_decision (memory_c5) misreads the situation, since that memory concerned a non-critical service on month-to-month terms while this contract does not auto-renew and lapsing it would leave the constrained line uncovered. If the memory_c2 record comes back showing a comparable component at comparable utilization with buffer-free onboarding, I would reweight toward switch_primary_vendor or toward staging the low-cost vendor as a second source first.
